bull_bear.body: Net cash INR 4,300cr; Management consciously holding high cash reserves to de-risk solution rollout; No M&A/buyout plans currently; Dividend policy standard; Focus on organic scaling before deploying excess capital.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global shipping volatility and geopolitical protectionism (antidumping duties); Delay in scaling new solution adoption beyond pilot sites; Currency reversal impacting realization; Sulfuric acid shortages in copper smelting (management deems impact minimal).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'business as usual' for financials but 'strategic shift' for growth; Reluctant to quantify volume impact prematurely but confident in medium-term trajectory; Transparent about one-offs.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'discharge system' is not a standalone product but an engineering layer that creates stickiness, allowing AIA to bypass commodity pricing discussions and antidumping hurdles by tying value to customer throughput gains (15%+ improvement).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Mining volume 45kt (Q4), 160kt (FY26); Non-mining 25kt (Q4), ~98kt (FY26); Realization INR 178/kg (Q4, peak due to mix/FX), sustainable guide INR 165/kg; Castings volume increasing but capacity utilization remains ~55%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need to improve ore throughput and reduce power consumption amid declining ore grades without massive capex. | Vedanta Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Large copper/zinc miner with aging assets; AIA's solution directly addresses throughput bottlenecks in ball mills. |
| Rising energy costs and lower ore grades impacting margins in gold/copper operations. | Hindustan Zinc | beneficiary | Med | Part of Vedanta group; potential candidate for mill optimization solutions to offset grade depletion. |
| Competitors relying on traditional wear-part sales may lose share if AIA's solution becomes industry standard. | JSW Steel (Cement/Mining arm) | loser | Low | While primarily steel, any captive mining consumables division faces displacement risk if AIA captures solution contracts. |

business.body:

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin artificially elevated by FX; Underlying operating margin ~28-29% excluding other income; Power cost ~5.8% of sales, expected to drop structurally as captive renewable capacity (100MW target) reaches 60-65% of consumption by June/July.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Volume-led acceleration expected post-FY27 as solution scales; Margin: Sustainable operating margin ~24-26% (excluding other income) as mix shifts to high-volume grinding media; Order inflow: Strong traction in linings converting to media; Capex: INR 100-150cr (maintenance + renewable balancing).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Specific quantum undisclosed due to confidentiality; Management confirmed immediate follow-on order for second mine conversion at the same customer post-trial success; Inventory up 25% YoY due to billing cycle shifts and stockpiling for South American orders.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 800kt-1Mt addressable market in gold/copper for discharge systems; Potential to replicate cement/platinum conversion trajectories where incumbents were displaced rapidly post-proof-of-concept; Capacity headroom to 70-75% utilization (~3.5L tons) before major greenfield capex.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: AIA Engineering reported record Q4 PAT driven by currency gains and mix, but the structural inflection is the successful validation of its 'new generation discharge system' at a marquee South American mine, shifting the narrative from commodity supplier to critical throughput partner. This proof-of-concept unlocks a previously inaccessible 800kt-1Mt addressable market, though volume monetization remains a 6-12 month lagging indicator.

open.item: Q4 realization ~178/kg (currency + product mix one-off); sustainable full-year realization ~165/kg going forward.
Renewables to supply ~60-65% of power once ~100 MW capacity comes online by June/July FY27.
Earlier ~15,000-ton South America (Chile) order dispatches started; regular invoicing stream from Q1FY27.
Second large-mine trial ongoing; outcome expected over the next couple of months.
Internal target to reach ~80% utilization of 440,000-ton capacity within 3 years (not a formal guidance).
FY27 outflow of 100-150 crores on maintenance capex and renewable balancing; ~30 cr balance to finish renewable portfolio.
Management believes volume can double from here over the next five years.
Continues holding high cash (~4,300 cr) despite ROCE drag; to consider reducing cash in 6-12 months.
Positions the liner + discharge-system + grinding media package as a unique multi-decade moat; design to be patented.
Operating margin (ex other income) ~28-29%; expected to trend to 24-26% as grinding-media mix rises with volume, though absolute profit grows.
China and Ghana plants (100,000 tons combined) on slowdown/paperwork status; can accelerate as needed, no firm timeline.
Global shipping volatility (transit +10-15 days) flagged as ongoing headwind but not a limiting factor; 100% pass-through.
Professional succession plan under implementation, to be formally in place over the next 1.5-2 years.
Acknowledges losing one large customer's volume to competition, a rare event; hopeful of correcting it.
Total capex for both China and Ghana plants estimated at USD 50 million using modular, automated technology.
Reiterates 1.5-2 million ton conversion opportunity intact; working on six-digit-ton opportunities across several mines.
Core strategy of converting the ~2.5 million ton forged grinding media market to high chrome, of which ~0.5 million already served by chrome.

verdicts.item: Expects to be back to 25,000-30,000-35,000 ton annual growth in a few quarters; rolling basis, FY25 as base.
verdicts.note: 'largely flat from full year last year' - growth run-rate not yet achieved.

verdicts.item: Declines to give FY26 volume growth guidance but reaffirms the 25,000-30,000 ton addition target is not abandoned.
verdicts.note: On FY27 'We are not giving any specific numbers... there are good things likely to come' - declines guidance while target not abandoned.

verdicts.item: China and Ghana plants delayed (land acquisition and approvals longer than estimated); plan/timeline update expected in next 1-2 quarters.
verdicts.note: 'Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode... under paperwork approval procedures' - timeline update provided.

verdicts.item: Confident of returning to normal growth from next fiscal (FY27); conversion news expected in coming quarters.
verdicts.note: 'We've gotten this important win' at a marquee South America customer; 'the volume journey for AIA will now start go forward... That is all our endeavor' - conversion news delivered, FY27 growth still…

verdicts.item: FY26 expected near-flat volume (between -5% and +15% vs last year); no specific growth guidance until end of Q2.
verdicts.note: 'full year sales of 258,000 tons, largely flat from full year last year, which was 255,000 tons' - within the -5% to +15% flat range.

verdicts.item: Hopeful of a South America (Chile copper) breakthrough in the next 2 quarters, flagged as a potential material game changer.
verdicts.note: 'we had a big breakthrough last month where one of a very marquee customer we implemented our solution'; 'they have immediately also given us the order for the second mine conversion' - breakthrough r…

verdicts.item: Mill liner business doing well, growing double-digit share of volume, with further expansions and investment.
verdicts.note: 'We have a good traction on the mill liners. We will only talk about the overall volumes' - no specific double-digit-share metric confirmed.

verdicts.item: US now carries ~9.6% ADD+CVD plus Section 232 tariff; customers paying the duty and business continues, but outcome uncertain.
verdicts.note: 'Status quo continues, as is' - US supply continues under duties.

verdicts.item: India capex outside the two overseas plants of ~100-130 crores (renewable, maintenance, land) for FY26.
verdicts.note: 'We spent about INR130 crores on capex' - within/near the 100-130 cr FY26 range.

verdicts.note: 'Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode. However, we can accelerate as and when needed' - Ghana timeline pushed out.
